2. The brief facts of the prosecution case is as follows:-
The case of the prosecution is that, Accused 1 to 6, together with the deceased accused No.7, with the common intention of defrauding Cw-1 by embezzling the property of plot number 40, located in Survey No. 5/4, 5/5, Pillaganahalli, Uttarahalli Hobli, within the jurisdiction of Konanakunte Police Station, Bangalore City and with the same intention of defrauding Cw-1, the accused No. 2, 3, 5 to 7 entered into a criminal conspiracy at the Upahar Banashree Hotel Service Hall on Bannerghatta Road.

Although the original owner of the said property, K.R.Rangappa, had passed away on 02.08.2011, in 1990, K.R.Rangappa had fake G.P.A. and certificate created in the name of Ramesh R. The accused No.5 brought old stamp papers and the accused No.7 had fake G.P.A. and certificate created.

The accused No.2 among the accused persons knew that his name was Krishnappa @ Kembathahalli Krishnappa, but as stated by Judgment 5 C.C. No.5360/2022 the accused No.6, he acted under the name of Ramesh R and registered the property of Cw-1, Plot No. 40, Survey No. 5/4, 5/5,
Uttarahalli Hobli, Pillaganahalli, which was not his property, in the name of Ramesh R S/o Ramajanappa, No. 33/34 Subhash Chandra Bose Road, Kadirenahalli Main Road, Banashankari, Bangalore City, in the name of the accused No.1, on 19.06.2018,

at the office of the Begur Sub- Registrar and the accused No.3 and 4 co-operated in registering the accused No.1 and signed the document in which the accused No.1 was registered as a witness and created records regarding the property belonging to Cw-1 as mentioned above, Cw-1 was deceived by creating documents regarding the property belonging to Cw-1.

As mentioned above, created documents regarding the property belonging to Cw-1 and use the said documents as real and thereby the accused persons have committed the above said alleged offences which are punishable U/s.120B, 419, 420, 465, 467,
471 R/w sec., 34 of IPC.

Charge has been framed and read over to the accused persons in kannada language, wherein they have denied the same and claim to be tried.
4. During the pendency of the case, the accused No.7 is reported to be dead and the case against the accused No.7 is abated/dropped.

sentences.text: Regarding the value of suggestions during the cross- examination and burden of proof concerned.

The Hon'ble High Court Gujarat in Legal Heirs of Umedmiya R Rathod Vs State of Gujarat, in First Appeal NO. 5952 of 1995 held as under:
Judgment 12 C.C. No.5360/2022 "74. ....

entities.text: Legal Heirs of Umedmiya R Rathod Vs State of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a settled position of law that mere suggestions are not sufficient to dislodge or disprove the case of the plaintiff.
Suggestions in cross- examination have no evidentiary value.

In absence of any evidence, nor any material traced in the cross examination in support thereof, the findings so far could not have been answered in the affirmative by the Trial Court as well as by this Court in the First Appeal.

78. The expression "burden of proof" is used in two senses, i.e. The burden of proving an issue or issues sometimes termed the 'legal burden', and the burden of proof as a matter of adducing evidence during the various stages of the trial.
What is called the burden of proof on the pleading should not be confused with the burden of adducing evidence which is described as "shifting".

See,
observations in Narayan v. Gopal [AIR 1960 SC 100]; Pickup v. Thames Insurance Co., [(1878) 3 QBD 594]; Lakshmana v. Venkateswarlu, [76 Ind APP 202 : (AIR 1949 PC 278); 15 Halsbury (Simond) 267]; HuytonwithRoby Urban District Council v. Hunter, [(1955) 2 All E. R. 398 at p. 400]
per Denning L. J.

sentences.text: These two aspects of the burden of proof Judgment 13 C.C. No.5360/2022 are enunciated in Sections 101 and 102 of the Evidence Act.
Section 101 shows that the initial burden of proving a prima facie case in his favor is on the plaintiff.
When he gives such evidence as will support a prima facie case, the onus shifts on the defendant to adduce rebutting evidence to meet the case made out by the plaintiff.
As the case continues to develop, the onus may shift back again to the plaintiff."
11. It is the paramount duty of the prosecution to establish the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubt.
Unless the guilt is established beyond all reasonable doubt, the accused persons can not be held guilty of the alleged offences.
12. In the present case, the Pw.1 is the complainant material witness has denied the alleged commission of the offences by the accused.
As such the accused, at the initial stage itself certainly would be entitled to benefit of the doubt, since material/injured witness has turned hostile to the prosecution case.
Judgment 14 C.C. No.5360/2022 On this point held in, (2016) 10 SCC 519 - AIR 2016 SC 4581 in para 56, Hon'ble Apex held thus hereunder:

It is a trite proposition of law, that suspicion however grave, it cannot take the place of proof and that the prosecution in order to succeed on a criminal charge cannot afford to lodge its case in the realm of ''may be true''' but has to essentially elevate it to the grade of ''must be true''.

In a criminal prosecution, the court has a duty to ensure that mere conjectures or suspicion do not take the place of legal proof and in a situation where a reasonable doubt is entertained in the backdrop of the S Venkatesh vs Dasamma on 9 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194840915/

available, to prevent miscarriage of justice, benefit of doubt is to be extended to the accused.

Such a doubt essentially has to be reasonable and not imaginary, fanciful, intangible or non-existent but as entertainable by an impartial,
prudent and analytical mind, judged on the touchstone of reason and common sense.

It is also a primary postulation in criminal jurisprudence that if two views are possible on the evidence available one pointing to the guilt of the accused and the other to his innocence, the one favourable to the accused ought to be adopted.''
Judgment 15 C.C. No.5360/2022 13.
Thus, the above Hon'ble Apex Court decision has opt to the present case on hand and the accused persons are entitled to the benefit of the reasonable doubt.
The Pw.1 is the complainant/witness not stated anything against the accused persons and have turned hostile to the prosecution case.

Hence, this court rejected the prayer of the learned Senior APP to examine other charge sheet witnesses, as no purpose would be served in examining them and also the valuable time of the court would be saved.

In view of the Pw.1 complainant/material witness was turned hostile to the prosecution and compromise is reported by the parties, the prosecution has not able to prove the alleged offences beyond all reasonable doubt.
Therefore, I answer to the Point No.1 to 6 in the Negative.
